chunks: And Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated from Dawud al-Sarimi who said:
I asked him about the drinker of wine (khamr), is he given something from the zakat? He said, 'No.'

key_terms.شَارِبِ الْخَمْرِ: Drinker of wine (a specific category of sinner)

ai.seo_question: Is a wine drinker eligible to receive zakat in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahid al-Ahkam* clarifies that a *sharib al-khamr* (wine drinker) remains eligible to receive zakat for poverty (*al-fuqara*), demonstrating that major sins do not automatically disqualify one from this form of financial aid. In Shia jurisprudence, this ruling underscores the principle that zakat is a right of the poor regardless of their moral status, provided they meet the financial criteria, serving as a mechanism for both relief and potential reformation.
